# before the rules existed) and the engine, waiting for review. The expected
# files are never edited to match the engine; TestExpectedFindings passes
# only while the engine's differences are exactly these lines, so a new
# difference, or one that disappears, fails it.
#
# Groups A-D of the Phase 4 review are resolved (A: defaults added to the
# expected files after checking that only defaults_used differed; B, C, D:
# fixtures and modelling changed as decided).
# E (scenario 6) is resolved in the third Phase 4 review: an edge costs its
#     cheapest fix side and a principal that can grant itself the access
#     again has no cut after it (SCORING.md §4); the engine gives the decided
#     cut (ASSUMES payments-api -> analytics-admin, identity side, cost 1),
#     and the fingerprint no longer depends on the cut (DESIGN.md §8).
# F (scenario 10) is resolved in the fourth Phase 4 review: a fix that
#     narrows a broad grant costs the side's price, one that revokes an
#     explicit grant 2 more (SCORING.md §4.1). The engine gives the decided
#     cut (the key policy's Principal "*" grant, narrow, cost 2; the explicit
#     read is the alternative, revoke, cost 3).
#
# No difference is open.
#
# G (Phase 6 review, 01_classic/key_outside_input) is resolved by the
#     decisions of the Phase 6 review: alternative_fix is the cheapest
#     complete cut sharing no edge with the chosen one, and a side resting
#     only on an unknown Allow is resolved (SCORING.md 4.1, 4.3).
#
# H (Phase 6 review, rounds 2-7) is resolved: the engine implements one
#     finding per rule, dominance with merged cuts, the unified alternative,
#     resolve and detach steps, the token as a revoke, the CAN_ESCALATE kind
#     in the notation and same-account update-trust, and matches every hand
#     derivation of the group but one (I).
#
# I (Phase 6 review, scenario 22 vulnerable, CLAPA-PATH-002). The hand
#     derivation gave ASSUMES role/app -> role/ops an identity side (role/app's
#     sts:AssumeRole names role/ops: revoke, 3). role/ops's trust names
#     role/app's ARN in the same account, and DESIGN.md 6 (the table "Same-
#     account effect of a resource-based policy", IAM User Guide) says an
#     implicit deny in the identity policy does not limit a same-account
#     resource policy naming an IAM role ARN: the trust alone grants, so the
#     identity side does not count (SCORING.md 4.1: a side counts only if the
#     decision no longer grants without it). The edge's only side is the
#     trust (revoke, 7); the engine's cut is CAN_ESCALATE[iam:modify-policy]
#     role/ops (revoke, 4) and its alternative the IRSA trust (7, tied with
#     the ASSUMES trust and closer to the entry). The derivation, not the
#     engine, departs from the documented rule; waiting for a decision.
